# Responsible AI note

**Privacy.** No real or personal customer data is used: all homes, usage and sales are synthetic, generated by documented rules. Customer memory (completed and declined retrofits, budget, disruption limit) is stored locally in `data/memory/` and holds no personal details. Only free LLM tiers are used, and the facts sent to them contain no name, address or postcode — only the region, home features and engine results. API keys live in a git-ignored `.env`.

**Bias and fairness.** Energy-model errors are reported by region, property type and age band, and on an out-of-distribution test set (one region and one age band never seen in training). Electricity error is even across groups: 19.5–22.8% by region, 20.2–22.0% by property type and 20.5–23.8% by age band; the out-of-distribution set (21.4%) is close to the in-distribution test set (20.9%). Homes are ranked by improvement potential (percentage reduction), not total consumption, so large homes are not marked inefficient for size alone. Tenants are not shown installations they cannot authorise.

**Explainability.** The Green Home Score is a fixed weighted sum with documented, monotonic sub-score mappings (`docs/scoring.md`); the dashboard shows every component's points earned out of points available, its input and whether it was recorded, metered, estimated or modelled. Each retrofit comes with a plain reason (e.g. "loft insulation is under 100 mm"), its prerequisites, and why unsuitable options were excluded. Savings are reported per fuel, so an electricity rise after a heat pump is shown, not hidden.

**Hallucination control.** The LLM never computes. It only (1) converts a question into a schema-validated scenario, which the engine reruns, and (2) explains a facts object built from the engine's results. A verifier blocks any number not present in those facts (allowing rounding and formatting); after one failed rewrite a deterministic template answers instead. On 57 held-out questions the verifier passed every answer, but a manual audit found groundedness 70.2%, factual accuracy 78.9% and unsupported claims in 5.1% of sentences — below our 90/90/<5% targets, mainly from unrequested follow-up questions and wording errors. We report this openly and treat it as the main open issue.

**Human oversight.** Every output is labelled an estimate, not a guarantee, with a confidence tier (A metered, B partial, C estimated), P10–P90 ranges and a *provisional* flag when inputs were guessed. Missing or conflicting key inputs produce a specific question instead of a guess. The dashboard states that a qualified assessor should confirm before any work; tenants see fabric advice marked as needing landlord consent and major installations marked as the owner's decision.

**Data limitations.**
- Labels come from our own physics simulator. High agreement shows the models reproduce the simulator from noisy, partly missing inputs; it does not establish real-world accuracy. Calibration to NEED-style medians is plausibility evidence only.
- Reference values (U-values, energy prices, emission factors, retrofit costs, consumption medians) are documented placeholders to be replaced from official sources (`docs/data_sources.md`).
- Our rating is an EPC-style approximation of SAP, not an official EPC; where a recorded rating exists, projected ratings are anchored on it.
- Property-value uplift comes from a model trained on synthetic sales, labelled *DEMO ONLY*. It is an observational association, not a causal effect, and is shown only as a range.
- Money is calculated internally and shown in rupees at a placeholder exchange rate (`data/reference/currency.json`); converted figures are not local market prices or tariffs.
